title: Equilibrium is the minimum of G
caption: As a reaction A ⇌ B proceeds, the Gibbs energy of the mixture falls to a minimum and then rises. The minimum is the equilibrium position. With ΔG° = −5 kJ mol⁻¹ at 298 K it lies at 0.88 of the way to products, where K = 7.5.
alt: Gibbs energy of the mixture against extent of reaction from pure A (0) to pure B (1): a curve with a minimum at about 0.88.
description: At 0, pure A; at 1, pure B, 5 kJ mol⁻¹ lower.
Mixing lowers G, so the curve dips below both ends.
The minimum, at 0.88, is equilibrium; the reaction moves downhill to it from either side.

checks.name: G is lowest at extent 0.883, where B/A = K = exp(−ΔG°/RT) = 7.52
